_comment: THE CLOSED INVENTORY of `paint_class` names, for FeedCodeSpan.paint_class
and FeedMergeTestSpan.paint_class in frontend/v1/feed.proto. The daemon
emits ONLY names listed here — its ANSI parser and its syntax highlighter
both assert their emitted classes against this file, so a class that
drifts out of the inventory fails at the producer rather than arriving
A CLIENT TREATS AN UNKNOWN CLASS AS UNSTYLED TEXT, NEVER AN ERROR. The
text is always the substance and the class is always decoration, so a
client that has not caught up with a newly added class must still draw
the span — dropping it, or throwing, would lose output the user needs to
read over a styling detail they do not.
THE EMPTY STRING MEANS PLAIN, and is the only value with that meaning:
a span with no styling carries "", never a 'plain' or 'default' class
name, so there is exactly one spelling of unstyled text on the wire.
This file pins the NAMES, not their appearance. Each renderer keys its
own stylesheet or face table off these names, and a webapp and an Emacs
buffer are free to draw 'keyword' differently.
_ansi_comment: The SGR-derived classes: what the daemon's ANSI parser produces from
escape sequences in captured process output (a merge run's test output
is the case that forced them). THE CLIENT NEVER PARSES ESCAPES — the
daemon does it once, and the client paints classes.
Six attribute classes, then a foreground and a background class for each
of the eight base colors and their eight bright variants. Listed one by
one rather than as a template: the inventory is closed, and a template
would make it a rule a consumer has to re-derive instead of a set it can
_syntax_comment: The highlight classes the daemon's syntax highlighter emits for a code
block's spans. Deliberately a SMALL, LANGUAGE-NEUTRAL set: every
language the highlighter knows maps onto these names, so a stylesheet is
written once and never per-language, and 'added'/'removed' let a
highlighted block carry diff coloring without a second vocabulary.
_composition_comment: A SPAN CARRIES EXACTLY ONE CLASS. `paint_class` is a single string and
means it: there is no list, no space-separated set, and no client-side
ANSI ATTRIBUTE COMBINATIONS ARE EXPRESSED BY SPLITTING. Text that is
bold AND red becomes adjacent spans over the same run, one per class, in
'ansi_precedence' order — the daemon does the splitting, so the wire
carries a flat sequence and a client concatenating span texts always
'ansi_precedence' is the order the daemon splits in, strongest first:
color is what a reader sees before anything else, so foreground leads
and background follows, then the weight and shape attributes in the
order SGR itself numbers them. It is the daemon's ordering rule, not a
client's — a client renders the spans it is given, in the order given.
